trust_decision.summary: Which local account an external OIDC/SAML login maps to is decided by a string equality on the external subject (and provider id) in oidc_user_links/saml_user_links; on MySQL/MariaDB those columns inherit the case- and accent-insensitive utf8mb4_unicode_ci collation, so a subject that merely differs in case or accent resolves to the victim's local user id. The fix forces byte-exact comparison both in the four queries and in the column DDL.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the OIDC `sub` lookup; this is the first `WHERE oidc_subject = ? AND provider_id = ?` in the tree and the account-takeover decision is made by its result at lib/Application/Service/UserProvisioningService.php:88-98.

fix_sites.entry_point: none - internal infrastructure helper DbCompat::binaryCollation() called from the service constructor for every OIDC/SAML login
manual upgrade script run by the administrator (new sql/poweradmin-mysql-update-to-4.2.5.sql; the sibling commit adds the same file as ...-update-to-4.3.4.sql)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The web installer rebuilds every table from PHP field arrays and then applies the administrator's chosen db_collation as a table-level option, so it reads as setup plumbing that neither the shipped .sql schema nor the login path depends on - and the advisory only talks about the OIDC `sub` lookup, not about how a fresh install is created.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: E-mail based account linking is deliberately case-insensitive: provisionUser falls back to `SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ? AND active = 1` on the users table's CI collation, and UserManager::emailExists lowercases both sides on purpose. A fix that applies the binary collation to users.email or to every identity comparison stops a case-variant e-mail from linking to the existing account and breaks the duplicate-e-mail guard the pinned commit just made case-insensitive.

O6_input_shapes: subject differing only in letter case (e.g. victim vs Victim)
subject differing only in diacritics (e.g. victim vs victim-accented)
provider_id differing only in case or accent
both link tables: OIDC subject and SAML subject/name-id
both query roles: the find-existing-account lookup and the orphaned-link cleanup lookup

O8_uncovered_routes.route: linkOidcToExistingUser / linkSamlToExistingUser decide reuse-vs-insert with `WHERE user_id = ? AND provider_id = ?`; the fix hardened provider_id in the four lookups but left these two on the column's default collation, so on any table whose columns are still CI a case-variant provider_id is treated as the same link and the UPDATE overwrites the stored subject.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The query is already scoped by user_id, so a case-variant provider cannot select another account - it is link bookkeeping, not the login decision.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 230 lines past the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Legacy MySQL upgrade script still creates both identity tables with `COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci` at table level; the fix added a new 4.2.5/4.3.4 ALTER but left the 4.1.0 script that first creates oidc_user_links and saml_user_links.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The file is superseded by the later update scripts and the new query-level COLLATE protects the login even on an un-migrated database.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: sql/ directory, one file away from the shipped schema the fix edited

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A repository method such as findUserIdByExternalSubject() next to cleanupExternalAuthLinks() that does the same lookup with plain `=`, reachable from user administration.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Lookups are already being moved into repositories; a maintainer would place the subject query there and not think about collation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-field `collation` option beside the existing per-field `charset` option, so the installer can emit utf8mb4_bin on just the identity columns.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The builder already supports per-field CHARACTER SET; collation is the missing half and is exactly what the installer path needs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The same byte-exact requirement expressed with the project's existing idiom (`BINARY secret_key` on MySQL) for another externally supplied token.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the project's own precedent for the identical MySQL-vs-PostgreSQL/SQLite comparison problem, so a sibling that copies it is very plausible.

O9_family: authentication bypass by non-canonical string comparison of an external identity claim - external OIDC/SAML subject matched to a local account under a case/accent-insensitive collation (CWE-287 improper authentication, CWE-178 case sensitivity)

O10_build.toolchain: PHP >= 8.2 with ext-intl/gettext/openssl/pdo, composer (runtime vendor/ partially committed; PHPUnit 11 for tests)
services: MySQL or MariaDB - required to exercise the collation behaviour; SQLite and PostgreSQL compare byte-exact by default and cannot reproduce it
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/Infrastructure/Database/DbCompatTest.php holds pure string-output unit tests for the DbCompat helpers (no testBinaryCollation at the pinned commit); tests/unit/Application/Service/UserProvisioningServiceTest.php is reflection-only and never touches a database. There are no DB-backed tests for provisioning and none for the installer's table builder.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add ` COLLATE utf8mb4_bin` to the two subject lookups the report names (or only change the column DDL in sql/poweradmin-mysql-db-structure.sql) and stop there, leaving the orphan-cleanup queries, the provider_id comparisons and the installer-built schema on the default collation.

out_of_scope_notes: User deletion and admin user management touch the link tables only by user_id (lib/Infrastructure/Repository/DbUserRepository.php:304-317, lib/Domain/Model/UserManager.php:380), so no external-subject lookup exists there.
cleanupOrphanedAuthLinks() is public (lib/Application/Service/UserProvisioningService.php:765) but has no caller in the tree, so it is not a reachable route.
unverified: repo_mb could not be measured (no shell in this session); vendor/ is partially committed, so the tree is well over 5 MB but the exact size is unknown.

The installer's charset/collation dropdowns (install/collations.php:4-13) allow utf8mb3 and latin1 values; on such an install the fix's hard-coded `COLLATE utf8mb4_bin` is a charset mismatch for the column and MySQL would raise, an error the catch in findUserByOidcSubject/findUserBySamlSubject swallows. Not verified against a live MySQL.
utf8mb4_bin is a PAD SPACE collation in MySQL, so a trailing-space variant of a subject may still compare equal; not verified against a live MySQL.
Whether hidden behavioural tests can drive the installer's table builder (it needs a MySQL service) is unknown.
Latest release given as none, so present_in_latest for the O8 routes is unknown.
